title: Terraform module for telemetry stack in VPC: Prometheus + Grafana + OTel Collector + log forwarder
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a reusable Terraform module to install and manage a telemetry stack inside customer VPC/k8s private deployments. The module will provision Prometheus and Grafana (via Helm), an OpenTelemetry Collector configured with OTLP and Prometheus receivers, and a lightweight log forwarder (Fluent Bit) to ship container logs. Goals: consistent defaults for private deployments, safe upgrade path, built-in health checks and integration tests, and clear inputs for integrations with customer KMS, service accounts, and network ACLs.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes clear inputs/outputs and works with Redwood private k8s clusters (EKS/GKE-like): chart versions, namespace, RBAC principals, scrape configs, retention settings.
Module deploys Prometheus and Grafana via Helm charts and creates ServiceMonitors/service discovery for core Redwood services.
OpenTelemetry Collector runs as a Deployment with OTLP receiver and Prometheus receiver; exports to local Prometheus remote_write and optionally to remote telemetry endpoints.
Fluent Bit daemonset configuration that forwards logs to either an internal log-aggregator endpoint or S3-compatible bucket with per-namespace filters.
Automated CI smoke test: terraform plan/apply in a disposable test VPC, basic scraping verification, Grafana dashboard rendering check, and log arrival confirmation.
Upgrade path documented and validated: canary rollouts for collector and fluent-bit, Helm value pinning, rollbacks tested with no metric loss >95%.
Health checks & alerts wired into runtime: liveness/readiness probes, Prometheus alert rules for scraping failures, and a synthetic job to verify metric end-to-end flow.
Module docs include example usage, troubleshooting steps, and recommended production settings for retention, sharding, and resource requests/limits.
implementation_notes: Module will prefer helm_release (Terraform Helm provider) for Prometheus and Grafana to keep compatibility with upstream charts and make upgrades predictable.
Provide an alternate k8s_manifest mode for installations that require CRD-first flows (when operator is present).
OTel Collector config templating: allow a minimal default config but accept a user-supplied config.raw string for advanced installs.
Default to Prometheus remote_write to a managed metrics ingest or to local TSDB; make remote_write optional via variable.
Fluent Bit recommended pipeline: kubernetes filter -> record_modifier -> output (http to log-aggregator or s3). Add option for gzip/compression and batching.
Expose metrics about the telemetry stack (scrape success ratio, collector CPU/memory, fluent-bit backlog) to the platform dashboard.
Module should create Kubernetes ServiceAccounts with minimal permissions and document required IAM role bindings for cloud providers.
Implement a canary upgrade helper: toggle to deploy a second collector replica set in a separate namespace with subset of traffic for a short window, then promote.
Add terraform test harness in GitHub Actions using kind/EKSctl ephemeral clusters and terratest scripts to validate plan/apply and smoke checks.

risks: Upgrades for prometheus-operator or kube-prometheus-stack can require CRD migrations; need careful sequencing to avoid downtime.
OTel Collector misconfiguration can drop metrics; must provide safe defaults and integration tests to catch regressions.
Log forwarding to external endpoints may expose credentials—KMS integration and secret handling required.
Resource sizing: undersized defaults could cause metric/backlog loss in noisy tenants; must provide conservative defaults and autoscale guidance.
next_steps: Finish terratest/GHA smoke tests that validate end-to-end metric and log flow in ephemeral clusters.
Complete security review and finalize RBAC/KMS guidance in the module README.
Add canary upgrade helper implementation and document rollback steps.
Schedule staging rollout for one dedicated customer cluster and monitor for metric continuity during upgrade.
